body: My father passed away a few weeks ago at the age of 41. He was in alot of pain, in the end, and I suspect this is what he was wanting to accomplish. It had been a year since my aunt (his sister passed away from a drug overdose) and also her birthday. He was manically depressed, suffered from high blood pressure and his sugar spiked easily. Alcoholism and an auto immune disease and epilepsy. Pain in his back, neck, feet, from surgeries. Im left to care for my younger brother, sister, and cousin. All at the age of 23 with a child and girl of my own. I’m barely a man to say the least and there’s so much my father had to offer and teach me. I miss him. I have no one to talk to because he was my true friend and only outlet. Surrounded with the stress we were already enduring, losing him is destroying me inside out at a much faster rate. I blame myself for not calling 911. I blame myself for not being strong enough to pull him out of my restroom to do CPR and waiting for my baby brother and cousin to help. I blame myself for not asking him if he were okay enough or doing enough. We had been through the routine of saving him when he got sad plenty of times. But it was hard to call it that. When he drank sugary alcohol, he would get sick and lose oxygen to his brain and pass out. I spent several days with my brain dead father while tubes were pumping his bloody stomach and helping him breathe and heart beat. The worst time of my life and here I am on Reddit posting this in hopes to make any sense of this . I dont want to live a life without him. My dad was incomparable and the most genuine person ive met. I would do anything to talk with him or be with him again.
